'''Papadam''' (also '''papadum''', '''poppadom''', '''papar''', and '''appalam''') is an [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] and [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Sri Lanka|Sri Lankan]] [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]].  Typically, it is prepared using [[Cookbook:Urad Bean|black gram]] bean flour, [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]], or [[Cookbook:Lentil|lentil]] flour with [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] and [[Cookbook:Peanut Oil|peanut oil]] added. The ingredients are made into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] and formed into a thin, round shape similar to a [[Cookbook:Tortilla|tortilla]]. As the dough is prepared, the papadam can be seasoned with a variety of different ingredients such as [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chilies]], [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], or other [[Cookbook:Spices and herbs|spices]].

Papadams are cooked by deep-frying in oil, which causes them to expand and crispen. They may also be cooked by roasting them over an open flame, in a toaster oven, or in a [[Cookbook:Microwave Oven|microwave oven]].   Depending on the cooking method they may be either soft and moist or crisp in texture.

Usually served as a complement to a main dish in South Asia, a relatively recent Western practice is to treat them as a [[Cookbook:Snacks|snack]] or as an [[Cookbook:Appetizers|appetizer]] to be topped with [[Cookbook:Chutney|chutney]], various dips or [[Cookbook:Salsa|salsas]]. Commonly made in different sizes, the smaller ones are for snacks and the larger variety may be used as a food wrap. 

== Ingredients==

*8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Urad Bean|black gram]] flour
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] cracked [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
*1 tsp ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin seeds]]
*½ tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Water|water]] (or more if needed)
*[[Cookbook:Oil|Oil]] for frying

== Procedure ==

# Mix together the flour, pepper, cumin, and salt.
# Add water and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] the [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] until it is smooth. You may have to add some water, depending on the flour.
# Split the dough into 10–15 balls.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] one ball at a time to a very thin round layer on a slightly oiled surface.
# Dry the papadams in the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] for an hour (at about 100°C or 200°F).
# Keep them in an airtight container.
# [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] the papadams in oil until they are crispy but not too brown.
